rationale: Rename the existing REC Solar record to its current public brand, REC Power, while preserving REC Solar and supported legal and historical names as aliases. Supersede the census's queued ADD_OWNER because ArcLight Capital is a shortened label for the existing ArcLight Capital Partners organization and the production record already has the correct single manager-level ownership period. Normalize ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P. into the fund field, clear the unsupported legal-vehicle field, and leave stake undisclosed. Retain the 2023 closed-active entry year based on the October 4, 2023 legal closing. Add the current website and San Luis Obispo headquarters, broaden the operating description to the current distributed-power model, replace the unsupported 2025 milestone date with the June 2026 rebrand, add the July 2026 operating-portfolio acquisition, and retain exactly one primary citation. No REC Power-level sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 15, 2026.

afterImage.name: REC Power
afterImage.description: REC Power, formerly REC Solar, is a nationwide independent power producer that develops and acquires, finances, owns, operates and services distributed power assets spanning solar, battery storage, fuel cells, microgrids and gensets for commercial, industrial, institutional and public-sector customers. Founded in 1997, the platform reports more than 700 projects across 29 states and, after a July 2026 acquisition, more than 410 MW of operating assets across 25 states. Duke Energy completed the sale of its commercial distributed-generation business, including REC Solar, to an ArcLight-managed investment fund in October 2023. REC Power states that it remains owned by ArcLight Capital Partners, and ArcLight attributes the investment to Fund VII. Public sources do not disclose the platform-level stake or legal acquisition vehicle.

REC Power completed the acquisition of fifteen operating distributed-generation solar projects totaling 68 MW, increasing its operating portfolio to more than 410 MW across 25 states.
